1. (a) Identify the lines and explain with reference to the context:
My heart's so harden'd I cannot repent.
Scarce can I name salvation, faith or heaven,
But fearful echoes thunders in my ears
Faustus thou art damn'd';
(b) Write a short note on the significance of the Pope scenes in Doctor Faustus. (10)
2. (a) Identify the lines and explain with reference to the context:
Come, you spirits,
That tend on mortal thoughts, unsex me here,
And fill me, from the crown to the toe, top-full
Of direst cruelty! make thick my blood,
Stop up th' access and passage to remorse;
(b) Write a short note on the porter scene in Macbeth.
3. (a) Identify the lines and explain with reference to the context:
Yes, I am poor. But I'm a gentleman,
And one that scorns this baseness which you practice.
Poor as I am I would not sell myself,
No, not to gain your charming high-prized person.
Though I admire you strangely for your beauty,
Yet I contemn your mind.
(b) Write a short note on Walter Blunt in The Rover.
